haiku-low.q1: Each hold lasts 10 minutes. If unclaimed, the Inventory timer releases it back on sale; the order stays Awaiting payment until the webhook decides.
haiku-low.q2: Before payment is requested. If any line is short, nothing is held, the order is Rejected, short items are shown, and no payment is requested.
haiku-low.q3: The charge uses the order id as idempotency key. The provider makes at most one charge per key, so a resent request cannot charge twice.
haiku-low.q4: If any line is gone, the refund is requested for the full amount, the order is Cancelled (out of stock), and the customer is emailed.
haiku-low.q5: Cart is emptied only after the order is Confirmed, when Cart reads OrderConfirmed. If checkout fails, the cart stays exactly as it was.
haiku-low.q6: Order moves each checkout through its steps and owns the order. Its status, stored in Order DB, records how far a checkout has got.
haiku-low.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment. Payment stores the outcome and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker, which Order reads.
haiku-low.q8: Payment stores each event id with the charge status in one transaction and ignores repeat webhooks. Order ignores a repeat PaymentSucceeded once Confirmed or Cancelled.
haiku-low.q9: Triggered by the provider's webhook: Payment stores the charge Declined and publishes PaymentDeclined. Order then asks Inventory to release the hold.
haiku-low.q10: Claim checks each hold is Held and unexpired. If not, one all-or-nothing re-reserve: every line available means Confirm; any line gone means refund.
haiku-low.q11: Refund stays Open in Payment DB; Payment retries the provider call with the same order-based key until the provider confirms, then marks it Refunded.
haiku-low.q12: Cart reads the OrderConfirmed event that Order publishes when it confirms an order, and empties the cart.

sonnet.q1: A hold lasts 10 minutes. If not claimed, the Inventory timer marks it Released and the stock goes back on sale (and an expired hold is invalid at claim even if the timer hasn't marked it yet).
sonnet.q2: Stock is held before any payment is requested. If any line is short, nothing is held (all-or-nothing transaction), order is Rejected, short items shown, no payment requested, cart unchanged.
sonnet.q3: The idempotency key (the order id) is sent with the charge; the provider makes at most one charge per key, so the resent request cannot charge twice.
sonnet.q4: Order asks Inventory to re-reserve every line once; if any line is gone, Order asks Payment to refund the full amount (refund stored Open, then provider refunded), and the order is set to Cancelled (out of stock) with an email to the customer.
sonnet.q5: The cart is emptied only after the order is Confirmed (when Cart reads OrderConfirmed). On any failure (rejected, failed, declined, cancelled) the cart stays unchanged.
sonnet.q6: Order drives the flow, mostly via HTTP calls and events on the broker; the record of progress is the order status stored in Order DB (Order owns the order).
sonnet.q7: The provider sends a webhook to Payment; Payment stores the outcome and publishes PaymentSucceeded or PaymentDeclined on the broker, which Order reads.
sonnet.q8: Webhooks: Payment checks the provider's event id; if already stored it ignores the webhook and answers OK (event id and charge status stored in one transaction). Events: Order ignores PaymentSucceeded if the order is already Confirmed or Cancelled; repeated claim/re-reserve changes nothing.
sonnet.q9: The hold is released. Payment publishes PaymentDeclined; Order reads it, sets Payment declined and asks Inventory to release the hold. If that request fails, nobody retries and the 10-minute expiry timer releases it.
sonnet.q10: At claim, Inventory checks each hold is Held and unexpired. If all valid, claim and confirm. If any is not valid, Order asks Inventory to re-reserve all lines once, all-or-nothing: if all available, holds are remade, claimed and order confirmed; if any line is gone, refund the full amount and cancel.
sonnet.q11: The refund record stays Open and Payment retries with the same refund key until the provider confirms, then it becomes Refunded. It is tracked in Payment DB, where it stays visible (never dropped).
sonnet.q12: Order publishes OrderConfirmed on the broker when it confirms the order; Cart reads that event and empties the cart (Cart service does it).
